# Pair Addresses

Compute deterministic Uniswap v2 pair addresses with CREATE2 and verify pair ordering and factory inputs.

## [getPair](https://developers.uniswap.org/docs/protocols/v2/guides/getting-pair-addresses\#getpair)

The most obvious way to get the address for a pair is to call `getPair` on the factory. If the pair exists, this function will return its address, else `address(0)` (`0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000`).

- The "canonical" way to determine whether or not a pair exists.
- Requires an onchain lookup.

## [CREATE2](https://developers.uniswap.org/docs/protocols/v2/guides/getting-pair-addresses\#create2)

Thanks to some [fancy footwork in the factory](https://github.com/Uniswap/uniswap-v2-core/blob/master/contracts/UniswapV2Factory.sol#L32), we can also compute pair addresses _without any onchain lookups_ because of [CREATE2](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1014). The following values are required for this technique:

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| `address` | The factory address |
| `salt` | `keccak256(abi.encodePacked(token0, token1))` |
| `keccak256(init_code)` | `0x96e8ac4277198ff8b6f785478aa9a39f403cb768dd02cbee326c3e7da348845f` |

- `token0` must be strictly less than `token1` by sort order.

- Can be computed offline.
- Requires the ability to perform `keccak256`.

## [Examples](https://developers.uniswap.org/docs/protocols/v2/guides/getting-pair-addresses\#examples)

### [Solidity](https://developers.uniswap.org/docs/protocols/v2/guides/getting-pair-addresses\#solidity)

```
address factory = 0x5C69bEe701ef814a2B6a3EDD4B1652CB9cc5aA6f;
address token0 = 0xCAFE000000000000000000000000000000000000; // change me!
address token1 = 0xF00D000000000000000000000000000000000000; // change me!

address pair = address(uint160(bytes20(keccak256(abi.encodePacked(
  hex'ff',
  factory,
  keccak256(abi.encodePacked(token0, token1)),
  hex'96e8ac4277198ff8b6f785478aa9a39f403cb768dd02cbee326c3e7da348845f'
))));
```
